disclaimer: Fees, visa rules, work-rights and test formats change often, and several destinations have tightened student rules recently. The figures below are indicative ranges to help you compare options; always confirm on the official government, university and test-body websites before you apply or pay.

countries.name: United States
countries.summary: The largest choice of universities and research funding, with a flexible liberal-arts undergraduate system.
countries.intakes: Fall (August/September) is the main intake; some universities also admit in Spring (January).
countries.tests: SAT or ACT (many universities are test-optional, but some require scores), TOEFL / IELTS / Duolingo; GRE or GMAT for many master's and MBA programmes.
countries.cost: Indicative tuition from roughly USD 20,000 to 60,000+ per year, plus living costs; public universities are usually cheaper for in-state students.

work.name: OPT and STEM OPT
work.detail: Up to 12 months of Optional Practical Training after a degree; STEM-designated degrees can get a 24-month extension, so up to 36 months in total.

countries.scholarships: Fulbright, university merit and need-based aid, teaching or research assistantships for master's/PhD.
countries.tip: Apply through the Common App for undergraduate and individual portals for graduate programmes; start 12 months ahead.

countries.name: United Kingdom
countries.summary: Shorter degrees: usually 3-year bachelor's and 1-year master's, which lowers total cost and time.
countries.intakes: September is the main intake; January and May intakes exist for some master's programmes.
countries.tests: IELTS (Academic) or other approved English tests; GRE/GMAT only for some programmes; undergraduate applications go through UCAS.
countries.cost: Indicative tuition from roughly GBP 15,000 to 38,000 per year depending on subject and university; London is the costliest city.

work.name: Graduate Route
work.detail: Currently 2 years of post-study work after a bachelor's or master's (3 years after a PhD). The UK government has announced a reduction for future applicants, so check the latest rule on gov.uk.

countries.scholarships: Chevening, Commonwealth Scholarships, university awards such as GREAT scholarships.
countries.tip: A UCAS personal statement is mandatory for undergraduate applications; deadlines for Oxford, Cambridge and medicine are earlier than for other courses.

countries.name: Germany
countries.summary: Public universities charge little or no tuition for most programmes, including for international students, which makes it the best-value option for engineering and sciences.
countries.intakes: Winter semester (October) is the main intake; Summer semester (April) for some programmes.
countries.tests: English-taught programmes need IELTS/TOEFL; German-taught programmes need German (TestDaF / DSH / Goethe). Indian applicants must obtain an APS certificate. Some programmes ask for GRE.
countries.cost: Most public universities charge no tuition (a semester contribution of a few hundred euros applies); Baden-Württemberg charges tuition for non-EU students. Students must show proof of funds, normally through a blocked account worth roughly EUR 11,000 to 12,000 per year.

work.name: 18-month job-seeker permit
work.detail: Graduates can stay up to 18 months to look for a job related to their degree, and can switch to a work or EU Blue Card route once hired.

countries.scholarships: DAAD scholarships, Deutschlandstipendium, Erasmus+ and foundation scholarships.
countries.tip: Apply through the university or uni-assist; learning basic German helps with part-time work and daily life even for English programmes.

countries.name: Canada
countries.summary: Strong college and university system with practical, co-op-style programmes; immigration policy is changing quickly.
countries.intakes: Fall (September) is the main intake, with January and May intakes common at colleges.
countries.tests: IELTS Academic or TOEFL; GRE/GMAT for some graduate programmes; SAT is generally not required for Canadian undergraduate admission.
countries.cost: Indicative tuition from roughly CAD 15,000 to 40,000 per year, plus proof of funds for living costs, which has increased in recent years.

work.name: Post-Graduation Work Permit (PGWP)
work.detail: Usually up to 3 years depending on programme length and study field, if the institution is eligible; check the current field-of-study and language requirements.

countries.scholarships: University entrance awards, Vanier Canada Graduate Scholarships (PhD), and Lester B. Pearson scholarships at the University of Toronto.
countries.tip: The government has introduced study-permit caps and provincial attestation rules, so confirm that your chosen programme is eligible before applying.

countries.name: Australia
countries.summary: High-quality universities and strong student-support systems; a growing number of vocational pathways too.
countries.intakes: February and July are the main intakes; some universities add November.
countries.tests: IELTS, TOEFL or PTE; GRE/GMAT only for certain programmes.
countries.cost: Indicative tuition from roughly AUD 20,000 to 50,000 per year, plus living costs and proof of funds.

work.name: Temporary Graduate visa (subclass 485)
work.detail: Typically 2 to 4 years of stay after graduation depending on qualification; rules and eligibility for this visa have been tightened in recent updates, so verify them with the Department of Home Affairs.

countries.scholarships: University scholarships, Australia Awards (limited countries), Destination Australia.
countries.tip: Check the Genuine Student requirement and the updated financial-capacity evidence before you apply.

countries.name: Ireland
countries.summary: English-speaking EU country with a big technology and pharma hiring base, especially around Dublin and Cork.
countries.intakes: September is the main intake; January for a few programmes.
countries.tests: IELTS, TOEFL or equivalent; undergraduate applications go through the CAO for EU students and directly to universities for many international students.
countries.cost: Indicative tuition from roughly EUR 10,000 to 25,000 per year, with medicine and some others costing more.

work.name: Third Level Graduation Programme (stay-back)
work.detail: Up to 12 months after a bachelor's degree and up to 24 months after a master's or PhD for eligible students, to look for work or take employment.

countries.scholarships: Government of Ireland International Education Scholarship and university-specific awards.
countries.tip: Accommodation is limited and expensive in Dublin, so start looking as soon as you accept an offer.

countries.name: Singapore
countries.summary: A compact Asian hub with top-ranked universities, a close link to industry and a short flight home.
countries.intakes: August is the main intake; January for some programmes.
countries.tests: Undergraduate admission uses Class 12 results plus SAT/ACT or similar for some universities; IELTS/TOEFL for English proof; GRE/GMAT for many graduate programmes.
countries.cost: Indicative tuition from roughly SGD 17,000 to 40,000+ per year depending on university and course; tuition grants require a work-in-Singapore bond.

work.name: No dedicated post-study visa
work.detail: Graduates generally need an Employment Pass or S Pass from an employer; there is no automatic stay-back, so plan internships and job offers early.

countries.scholarships: Singapore International Graduate Award (research), ASEAN and university scholarships.
countries.tip: Competition for seats at NUS and NTU is very high; include strong extra-curricular and subject-based evidence in your application.

exams.name: IELTS
exams.purpose: English proficiency for the UK, Canada, Australia, Ireland and more (also accepted in the USA).
exams.format: Listening, Reading, Writing and Speaking; Academic version for university study; paper or computer-based.
exams.score: Band scale 0 to 9; most universities ask for 6.0 to 7.5 overall.
steps: Pick Academic or General Training (Academic for degrees).
Book through British Council or IDP.
Prepare using official practice material and timed mocks.
Send score reports directly to universities.

exams.name: TOEFL iBT
exams.full: Test of English as a Foreign Language, internet-based
exams.purpose: English proficiency, especially for the USA and Canada.
exams.format: Reading, Listening, Speaking and Writing; taken at a test centre or at home, depending on availability.
exams.score: Scored out of 120 (ETS has been updating the test and its score reporting, so check the current format).
steps: Check the university's minimum score and whether MyBest scores are accepted.
Register on the ETS website.
Prepare with ETS official practice tests.
Add university score recipients before or after the test.

exams.name: SAT
exams.purpose: Undergraduate admission in the USA and some other countries.
exams.format: Digital, adaptive; Reading and Writing plus Math.
exams.validity: Scores are generally accepted for several years; confirm each university's policy.
steps: Check whether your target universities require, recommend or ignore SAT scores.
Register on the College Board website; sit the test in Class 11 or early Class 12.
Practise in the official digital tool, Bluebook.
Send scores to universities (some allow self-reporting).

exams.name: GRE General Test
exams.purpose: Master's and PhD admission, mainly in the USA and also in Germany, Canada and Singapore for some programmes.
exams.format: Verbal Reasoning, Quantitative Reasoning and Analytical Writing; shorter than the older format.
exams.score: 130 to 170 for Verbal and Quant each; Analytical Writing 0 to 6.
steps: See whether your programme needs GRE (many have become optional).
Register on the ETS website.
Build a vocabulary and quant practice routine for 8 to 12 weeks.
Send official scores to chosen universities.

exams.name: GMAT
exams.purpose: MBA and business master's programmes worldwide.
exams.format: Quantitative Reasoning, Verbal Reasoning and Data Insights; computer-adaptive.
steps: Check the average GMAT of your target business schools.
Register on the official GMAC website.
Practise with the official prep material and mock tests.
Send scores to schools through the GMAC portal.

visa_guide.title: Post-study work visa
visa_guide.text: A post-study work visa lets you stay and work after graduating, so that you can recover the cost of your degree. Rules differ widely: Germany offers an 18-month job-seeker permit, the UK a Graduate Route, Canada a PGWP, Australia the 485 visa, Ireland a stay-back scheme and the USA OPT. Check duration, conditions and any recent changes before you pick a country.

visa_guide.title: STEM extension
visa_guide.text: The USA gives students with STEM-designated degrees a 24-month OPT extension on top of the first 12 months. Check that your exact programme (by CIP code) is on the official STEM-designated list, because a similar-sounding programme may not qualify.

visa_guide.title: Proof of funds
visa_guide.text: Most countries ask you to show savings or loan sanction that covers tuition and living costs for the first year or longer. Germany's blocked account and Canada's guaranteed investment certificates are examples. Start financial paperwork early.

visa_guide.title: Work during study
visa_guide.text: Most destinations allow limited part-time work during term and more during holidays, with different caps per country. Do not plan to fund your degree through part-time work alone.

scholarships.name: Fulbright-Nehru Fellowships and Fulbright programmes
scholarships.note: Competitive, merit-based awards; check each programme's eligibility and application window.

scholarships.name: Chevening Scholarships
scholarships.note: Typically needs at least two years of work experience and a plan to return home after the award; check the current rules.

scholarships.name: DAAD Scholarships
scholarships.note: Several programmes cover living costs; apply through the DAAD database and follow each programme's rules.

scholarships.name: Commonwealth Scholarships
scholarships.note: For students from eligible Commonwealth countries; check current categories.

scholarships.name: Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters
scholarships.note: Study in two or more European countries with an integrated scholarship; apply directly to each programme.

scholarships.name: Government of Ireland International Education Scholarship
scholarships.note: Competitive; open to non-EU students nominated through participating institutions.
